title: The Derivative: Speed at a Single Instant
hook: How fast is something moving at a single instant, when no time passes at all?
objectives: Interpret an average rate of change as the slope of a secant line.
Explain why the derivative is a limit rather than a division by zero.
Compute the derivative of x squared from the definition.

sections.title: A question about an instant
sections.goal: Create the puzzle of instantaneous speed.
sections.explanation: Average speed is distance over time. Shrinking the time interval to nothing turns the fraction into 0/0.
sections.visual_idea: A dot drives along a road; a brace marks the distance; the interval shrinks to a point and the fraction becomes 0/0.

sections.title: Slopes of secant lines
sections.goal: Connect average rate of change with the slope of a secant.
sections.explanation: Plot position as a curve. The average rate between x and x+h is the rise over the run of the line through the two points.
sections.visual_idea: Axes with a curve, two points, a rise-over-run triangle and the secant line.

sections.title: Let h shrink
sections.goal: See the secant slopes converge and name the limit.
sections.explanation: Sliding the second point toward the first, the secant pivots and its slope settles on one value; zoomed in, the curve looks straight. That value is the derivative.
sections.visual_idea: A value tracker shrinks h; readouts of h and the slope converge; the camera zooms in on the point; the tangent appears.

sections.title: An example: x squared
sections.goal: Use the definition on a concrete function and land the takeaway.
sections.explanation: For f(x) = x squared the difference quotient simplifies to 2x + h, so the derivative is 2x: a new function giving the slope everywhere.
sections.visual_idea: The algebra unfolds line by line; then a tangent line slides along a parabola with a live slope readout equal to 2x.

takeaway: The derivative turns the meaningless 0/0 into something precise: the slope of the curve - the rate of change - at every single instant.

quiz.question: The slope of the secant line through (x, f(x)) and (x+h, f(x+h)) measures...
choices: the average rate of change of f between x and x+h
the instantaneous rate of change of f at x
the area under the curve from x to x+h
the value of f at x+h
quiz.why: Rise over run across the interval is exactly an average rate of change.

quiz.question: If f(x) = x squared, what is f'(3)?
quiz.why: The derivative of x squared is 2x, and 2 times 3 is 6.

quiz.question: Why can't we just set h = 0 in (f(x+h) - f(x)) / h?
choices: It gives 0/0, which has no value
f is not defined at x
quiz.why: Both numerator and denominator become zero; the derivative is the limit as h approaches zero instead.
